def: The call auction before continuous trading. Orders are collected in the {{fact:mkt-preopen-window}} window, which ends at a random second in its last two minutes, and are then matched at one equilibrium price before the regular session opens. Index and current-month stock futures have had their own pre-open since {{date:2025-12-08}}, in the {{fact:mkt-fo-preopen-since}} window.

Normal order matching on price-time priority. For most stocks the window is {{fact:mkt-continuous-session}}; stocks that have derivatives trade continuously in the shorter {{fact:mkt-continuous-session-cas-stocks}} window and then enter the Closing Auction Session, an arrangement that changes on {{date:2026-12-07}} when every stock returns to the longer window.

A closing call auction for stocks that have derivatives, live since {{date:2026-08-03}} in the {{fact:mkt-closing-session}} window: a reference price is fixed first, orders are collected in the {{fact:mkt-cas-order-entry-current}} phase within a {{fact:mkt-cas-band}} band, and everything matches at one closing price. From {{date:2026-12-07}} the auction moves to the {{fact:opt-cas-window-from-2026-12-07}} window.

The price the closing auction starts from: the volume-weighted average of the last fifteen minutes of continuous trading. Auction orders must sit within {{fact:mkt-cas-band}} of it, and futures price bands line up with it while the auction runs.

The system picks the exact second an order-entry phase ends inside a published window, so nobody can time the last order. The cash pre-open order entry, in the {{fact:mkt-preopen-window}} window, ends at random in its last two minutes; the closing auction’s order entry ends the same way.

The exchange’s own after-hours window, {{fact:mkt-post-close-session}}, in which cash-segment orders are accepted and matched at the day’s closing price. It is not the broker’s after-market order facility.

Two short exchange windows for pre-negotiated large trades, {{fact:mkt-block-window-1}} and {{fact:mkt-block-window-2}}, with a minimum order of {{fact:sebi-block-deal-min-size}} and prices held within a narrow band of a reference price. Executed deals are published after the close.
An order to buy or sell at a stated price or better; it rests in the order book until it is matched or cancelled.
An order to trade now at the best available price. The fill is certain, the price is not, so slippage is largest in thin option strikes and in the first minutes after the open.
A limit order that enters the book only when a trigger price is touched; the trader sets both the trigger and the limit price.
A stop-loss order that becomes a market order when triggered: the exit is certain, the exit price is not. Many brokers block it for options.
A standing instruction kept by the broker, valid for months, that sends an order to the exchange when a trigger price is reached; it is not an exchange order until then.
A broker facility that queues an order outside market hours and releases it to the exchange in the next pre-open or at the open. A broker construct, not an exchange session.

An exchange order type that shows only part of its quantity in the order book and releases the rest in slices as the visible part fills; the undisclosed remainder never appears in market depth. Brokers also sell their own slicing feature under the same name, which splits one large order into legs that each stay within the freeze quantity. From {{date:2027-02-08}} unexecuted iceberg orders carry into the closing auction as fully disclosed limit orders.
Intraday order types that bundle the entry with a compulsory stop-loss (cover) and optionally a target (bracket); availability varies by broker since the 2021 peak-margin rules.
The broker product code for intraday positions, which the broker squares off before the close if the client has not exited.
The product code for carry-forward derivatives positions, which carry the full SPAN plus extreme loss margin.
The product code for delivery-based equity buying and selling from holdings: no leverage, settled on the {{fact:mkt-settlement-cycle}} cycle.

The broker’s forced closure of open intraday positions in a window before the close. One large broker starts at {{fact:mkt-squareoff-example-cash}} for cash and {{fact:mkt-squareoff-example-fo}} for derivatives, and charges {{fact:chg-rms-squareoff-example-broker}} when its risk desk does the closing.
The value-at-risk margin on cash-segment trades, sized to cover a likely one-day loss at a high confidence level; collected upfront together with the extreme loss margin.

An add-on margin covering losses beyond what VaR or SPAN estimates. On an index option’s expiry day, short positions in the expiring contracts carry an additional {{fact:fo-expiry-day-elm-addon}} ELM.
The portfolio-based initial margin for futures and options, computed from scenario losses (Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk) across a position’s legs.

Margin checked on random intraday snapshots rather than only at the end of the day. Since {{fact:sebi-peak-margin-since}} the full peak-snapshot margin must be collected, which ended broker-funded intraday leverage.

The rule that margin is collected before a trade: {{fact:sebi-upfront-margin-rule}} in the cash segment (with no short-collection penalty once at least {{fact:sebi-upfront-margin-waiver-threshold}} of the trade value is collected), SPAN plus ELM in derivatives and, since {{fact:opt-upfront-premium-since}}, the net option premium from buyers.
Shares and funds change hands one working day after the trade. The standard cycle for Indian equities is {{fact:mkt-settlement-cycle}}.
A same-day settlement segment, launched as a beta on {{date:2024-03-28}}, that runs alongside the regular cycle in a shorter trading window. Status today: {{fact:mkt-t0-segment-status}}.

The daily range outside which a stock cannot trade, set as a percentage of the previous close and varying by scrip; stocks with derivatives have dynamic bands that relax in steps instead of a hard limit.
Market-wide trading halts triggered when Nifty 50 or Sensex moves {{fact:mkt-index-circuit-breaker}} from the previous close, whichever index is hit first; the halt length depends on the time of day.
An exchange surveillance list for stocks with unusual price or volume behaviour. Listed stocks attract higher margins, often the full trade value, and brokers may withdraw intraday leverage on them.

A staged surveillance list for illiquid or suspect stocks. Higher stages add trade-for-trade settlement, tight price bands, an additional surveillance deposit and, at the top stage, trading only once a week.
A settlement mode in which every trade must result in delivery: no intraday netting of buys against sells, so a stock in this segment cannot be day-traded.
The cap on total open interest in a stock’s derivatives, set per stock as the {{fact:fo-mwpl-formula}} and measured in future-equivalent terms. It drives the F&O ban.

When combined open interest in a stock’s derivatives crosses {{fact:fo-mwpl-ban-threshold}} of its market-wide position limit, new positions are barred and trades may only reduce exposure until open interest falls back below the exit level.

Open interest restated as the equivalent number of futures by multiplying each option position by its delta; the basis on which index-option position limits and the F&O ban test are measured since 2025.

Settlement mode of stock derivatives at expiry: {{fact:fo-stock-fo-settlement}}. Stock futures and in-the-money stock options end in a transfer of shares rather than cash, so an unhedged position can require the full value of the shares.

The number of units in one derivatives contract (Nifty 50: {{fact:fo-nifty-lot}}; Bank Nifty: {{fact:fo-banknifty-lot}}; Sensex: {{fact:fo-sensex-lot}}). Lots are reviewed so that a new index contract is worth at least {{fact:fo-min-contract-value}}.

Index options that expire every week. Each exchange may list weeklies on only {{fact:opt-weekly-expiries-per-exchange}} benchmark index: NSE’s Nifty 50 on {{fact:fo-nifty-weekly-expiry-day}} and BSE’s Sensex on {{fact:fo-sensex-weekly-expiry-day}}. Bank Nifty weekly options: {{fact:fo-banknifty-weekly-status}}.
The {{fact:fo-monthly-expiry-day-nse}} on NSE and the {{fact:fo-monthly-expiry-day-bse}} on BSE, when monthly futures and options settle; stock derivatives are monthly only.

The maximum quantity one derivatives order may carry; a larger order is rejected and must be split. For Nifty 50 contracts it is {{fact:fo-freeze-qty-nifty}} and for Bank Nifty {{fact:fo-freeze-qty-banknifty}}, the figures in force since {{date:2026-11-02}}.

A central tax on exchange trades: {{fact:chg-stt-equity-delivery}} on each side of a delivery trade, {{fact:chg-stt-equity-intraday}} on the sell side of an intraday equity trade, {{fact:chg-stt-futures}} on futures sold, {{fact:chg-stt-options-sell}} of the premium on options sold and {{fact:chg-stt-options-exercise}} of intrinsic value when an option is exercised.

A state levy on the buy side at uniform national rates: {{fact:chg-stamp-delivery}} for delivery, {{fact:chg-stamp-intraday}} for intraday equity, {{fact:chg-stamp-futures}} for futures and {{fact:chg-stamp-options}} on option premium.

The fee the exchange charges members on turnover, passed on to clients. On NSE it is {{fact:chg-nse-txn-equity}} in the cash segment, {{fact:chg-nse-txn-futures}} on futures and {{fact:chg-nse-txn-options}} on option premium, each side.
The Investor Protection Fund Trust contribution, {{fact:chg-ipft-nse}} on NSE, folded into the exchange transaction charge rather than shown as a separate line.
A regulatory fee of {{fact:chg-sebi-fee}} on each side, passed through to clients. GST of {{fact:chg-gst-rate}} is charged on brokerage and on the exchange and SEBI charges, not on STT or stamp duty.
A depository-participant fee charged when shares leave a demat account on a delivery sale, per scrip per day whatever the quantity; one large broker charges {{fact:chg-dp-example-broker}}.
Reading trend from the sequence of swing points: higher highs and higher lows mean an uptrend, lower highs and lower lows a downtrend.
A move beyond the most recent swing high or low that contradicts the prevailing sequence, read as the first sign of a trend change.
Price zones where buying or selling has repeatedly stopped a move; traders watch for a reaction or a clean break there.
A quick push through an obvious level where stop orders cluster, followed by a reversal once those stops have been filled.

Volume-weighted average price: the sum of price times volume divided by total volume over a window, usually the session. Institutions use it as an execution benchmark, intraday traders as a fair-value line, and the closing auction’s reference price is a VWAP of the last fifteen minutes.
VWAP computed from a chosen bar, such as a swing low, a gap or an event day, rather than from the session open.
Entering when price leaves the high–low range of the first minutes of the session (commonly five, fifteen or thirty), with the stop inside the range or beyond its other side.
The open minus the previous close. A gap-and-go continues in the gap’s direction; a gap-fill trades back to the previous close.

Three lines from the previous session: pivot = (high + low + close) ÷ three, bottom central = (high + low) ÷ two, top central = twice the pivot minus the bottom central. A narrow range is read as a trending-day setup, a wide one as a range day.
Intraday levels (H1–H4 and L1–L4) placed at the previous close plus or minus 1.1 times the previous range divided by twelve, six, four and two; fades are taken at H3/L3 and breakouts past H4/L4.
An average of past closes that weights recent closes more; nine, twenty and fifty periods are common intraday settings. Like every average it lags price by construction.
Relative Strength Index (Wilder): a 0–100 momentum oscillator of average gains against average losses over a look-back of fourteen periods by default; extremes and divergences are the usual signals.

Moving average convergence/divergence (Appel): the difference between two EMAs (twelve and twenty-six periods by default) with a nine-period signal line; crossovers and histogram shifts show momentum change, with lag.
Price makes a new high or low while an oscillator does not, read as fading momentum. A practitioner signal without a located peer-reviewed test.

A twenty-period moving average with bands two standard deviations either side; BandWidth measures their spread, and a squeeze (unusually narrow bands) flags low volatility that often precedes expansion. Bollinger’s own rules treat closes outside the bands as continuation, not reversal.
Average True Range (Wilder): the average of the true range, which includes gaps, over a number of bars; a volatility unit for stops and targets, not a direction signal.
A histogram of traded volume by price level over a window; the high-volume node is where most business was done, the low-volume nodes where price moved through quickly.
Steidlmayer’s chart that stacks time-price opportunities (thirty-minute letters) by price; the value area holds about seventy per cent of the day’s TPOs and the shape classifies the session.
A trend line at the bar midpoint plus or minus a multiple of ATR that flips when price closes through the opposite band; it tracks trends but lags and whipsaws in ranges.
A stock’s or sector’s return compared with a benchmark such as Nifty 50 over the same window; not the RSI oscillator. Intraday traders buy leaders and sell laggards.
Money moving between sectors (banks, IT, metals and so on), visible as sector indices diverging from Nifty 50. Evidence exists at monthly horizons; intraday rotation is practitioner lore.
Deciding direction on a higher timeframe and timing the entry on a lower one, so the trade goes with the larger flow.

The resting limit orders at the best bid and ask prices: NSE shows {{fact:mkt-depth-levels-free}} price levels by default and {{fact:mkt-depth-levels-l3}} in the extended view. Market, stop-loss and undisclosed iceberg quantity are not in it; only the tick-by-tick feed carries the full book.

A session that opens near one extreme and closes near the other with few deep pullbacks. A narrow CPR and a wide opening drive are the usual tells, and it is the day on which pyramiding and holding into the close pay.
The right, not the obligation, to buy the underlying at the strike by expiry; buyers pay the premium, sellers receive it and carry the obligation.
The right to sell the underlying at the strike by expiry; it gains when the underlying falls.

The price at which an option can be exercised. Nifty 50 strikes are listed at an interval of {{fact:opt-strike-interval-nifty}} around the spot level, and option prices move in ticks of {{fact:opt-tick-size-options}}.
The option’s market price, made of intrinsic value plus time value, quoted per unit and multiplied by the lot size to get the cash amount.
Whether an option has intrinsic value (in the money), sits at the current price (at the money) or has none (out of the money).
The amount by which an option is in the money; zero for out-of-the-money options.
Premium above intrinsic value, paid for the chance of a favourable move before expiry; it decays to zero at expiry.
The number of contracts outstanding and not yet closed; one unit of OI is one buyer and one seller. Rising OI with a rising price shows new long positions, rising OI with a falling price new shorts.
The intraday or daily change in open interest at a strike; rising OI with price shows positions being added, falling OI shows unwinding.
Put open interest divided by call open interest for an expiry; read as a sentiment gauge, with extremes treated as contrarian.
The strike at which option buyers in aggregate lose the most at expiry; the claim that price gravitates there is contested.

The tendency of an underlying to close near a strike with large open interest on expiry day, attributed to market-makers’ delta hedging; documented in US data up to about 2009 and not found in later S&P 500 data. No Indian study exists.
The annualised volatility an option price implies when fed back through a pricing model; higher IV means richer premiums.
Where today’s IV sits against its own past year: the percentile is the share of days with lower IV, the rank is its position between the year’s low and high.

The tendency of implied volatility to exceed the volatility later realised, which is why selling options earns a premium on average and loses heavily in the rare tail; measured in US index options, not in a published Indian study.
The change in option price for a one-point move in the underlying; also a rough probability of finishing in the money, and the weight used to turn option positions into future-equivalent exposure.
The rate at which delta changes per point of the underlying; largest for at-the-money options close to expiry, which is why expiry-day premiums swing fastest.
The daily loss of option value from time passing, everything else equal; it accelerates into expiry.
The change in option price for a one-point change in implied volatility; longer-dated options carry more vega.
The market-implied one-standard-deviation range to expiry, approximated by the price of the at-the-money straddle.
The fall in implied volatility once a scheduled event (RBI policy, Budget, results, CPI, FOMC) is known; the premium that priced the uncertainty leaves the option even if price moves.

Trading options on their last day, when premiums are small, gamma is extreme and short positions in the expiring contracts carry an additional {{fact:fo-expiry-day-elm-addon}} ELM. In FY26 about {{fact:opt-zero-dte-share-fy26}} of index-option turnover was in same-day-expiry contracts.

A call and a put at the same strike and expiry. Sold (a short straddle), it profits if the underlying closes between the strike plus and minus the total premium, with unlimited risk either side unless hedged; bought, it needs a move larger than the premium paid.
An out-of-the-money call and put with the same expiry, sold or bought; wider break-evens and a smaller credit than a straddle.
Buying one option and selling another of the same type and expiry at a different strike, capping both risk and reward.

Defined-risk short-volatility structures. A condor sells an out-of-the-money call spread and put spread; a fly sells the at-the-money straddle and buys wings that cap the loss, which also cuts the margin.
Spreads with unequal legs or asymmetric wings that shift risk to one side in exchange for lower or zero cost.

Opposite positions in different expiries of the same underlying. Margin benefit on the pair: {{fact:opt-calendar-spread-expiry-rule}} (index contracts since {{date:2025-02-10}}, single stocks since {{date:2026-05-05}}).
A position whose net delta is near zero, so small moves in the underlying barely change its value; it needs re-hedging as delta drifts.
Pairing a short option with a long option in the same underlying so that SPAN margin falls sharply because the maximum loss is capped.

NSE’s index of expected thirty-day Nifty 50 volatility, derived from out-of-the-money near- and mid-month option prices by the CBOE method and quoted as an annualised percentage; a regime gauge for sizing.

Caps on index-option exposure measured in future-equivalent terms. End of day: {{fact:opt-position-limit-index-eod-net}} net and {{fact:opt-position-limit-index-eod-gross}} gross per PAN. Intraday, since {{date:2025-10-01}}: {{fact:opt-position-limit-index-intraday-net}} net and {{fact:opt-position-limit-index-intraday-gross}} gross per entity, checked on at least {{fact:opt-intraday-monitoring-snapshots}} random snapshots a day, with expiry-day breaches penalised since {{date:2025-12-06}}.
Adding to a winning position in steps, each addition protected by moving the earlier stop so that total open risk never exceeds the first unit’s risk.

Dollar-denominated Nifty 50 futures on NSE IX at GIFT City, trading in two sessions ({{fact:mac-gift-nifty-session-1}} and {{fact:mac-gift-nifty-session-2}}); its level before the Indian open is the usual read of the opening gap.
Foreign portfolio investor (the older term is FII). Daily net buying appears provisionally on NSE after the close and in final form on the depositories’ FPI monitors.
Domestic institutional investor: mutual funds, insurers, banks and pension funds. NSE publishes their net cash-market flow daily alongside the FPI figure.
The rupee’s exchange rate against the dollar. A weaker rupee helps IT exporters and hurts importers, and the RBI intervenes to smooth moves.
The daily USD/INR benchmark published by Financial Benchmarks India at {{fact:mac-usdinr-reference-rate-time}}, used for settlement and valuation.
ICE’s fixed-weight index of the dollar against six currencies, with the euro the largest weight; a rising DXY usually coincides with pressure on emerging-market currencies and flows.
The benchmark Treasury yield; rising yields raise the global discount rate and often weigh on Indian equities and foreign flows.

The US Federal Reserve’s rate-setting committee. Its statement is released at two in the afternoon Eastern Time, which is {{fact:mac-fomc-statement-ist-dst}} during US daylight saving time and {{fact:mac-fomc-statement-ist-std}} the next day in winter.
The RBI’s six-member committee that sets the repo rate, meeting six times a year; the Governor’s statement lands at {{fact:mac-rbi-mpc-time-ist}} on the last meeting day.

The RBI’s policy rate, at which it lends overnight against securities: {{fact:mac-repo-rate}}. The Standing Deposit Facility sits a quarter-point below it as the floor of the rate corridor and the Marginal Standing Facility a quarter-point above as the ceiling.

The retail inflation gauge. India’s is published by MoSPI on the twelfth of the month at {{fact:mac-india-cpi-release-ist}}; the US figure comes from the BLS at {{fact:mac-us-cpi-release-ist-dst}} in summer and {{fact:mac-us-cpi-release-ist-std}} in winter.

The US monthly jobs report, released by the BLS on a Friday at {{fact:mac-us-nfp-release-ist-dst}} during US daylight saving time and {{fact:mac-us-nfp-release-ist-std}} otherwise; a top-tier volatility event for global risk assets.

Brent is the global oil benchmark; the Indian basket is PPAC’s weighted average of the sour and sweet grades India buys. India imports about {{fact:mac-crude-import-dependence}} of its crude, so spikes hurt the rupee, the oil marketers and paint, aviation and tyre stocks.
A session with a scheduled high-impact release (RBI policy, Budget, CPI, FOMC, results) in which option premiums are inflated beforehand and positions should be sized smaller.

Three US trade-law routes to tariffs. Section 301 of the Trade Act targets unfair practices (a {{fact:mac-us-tariff-india-s301}} duty on most Indian goods since {{date:2026-07-24}}); IEEPA emergency powers were struck down for tariffs in February 2026; Section 122 allows a temporary surcharge for up to 150 days.
A client’s trades in one scrip in a day exceeding half a per cent of its listed shares; the broker discloses them and the exchange publishes them after hours.

A large pre-negotiated trade executed in a separate exchange window, with a minimum order of {{fact:sebi-block-deal-min-size}}, a price within a narrow band of the reference price and compulsory delivery.

Promoter shares given as collateral for a loan. Creation, invocation and release are disclosed to the exchanges within seven working days under the takeover regulations, and a rising pledge is a governance red flag.
The period in which a company’s insiders may trade; it closes from the end of a quarter until forty-eight hours after the results are public.

A transaction with promoters or affiliates that crosses the materiality threshold in the listing regulations needs audit-committee clearance and shareholder approval; the pattern of such deals is a governance signal.
EBITDA divided by revenue from operations. EBITDA is derived (profit before tax plus interest, depreciation and amortisation); it is not a line the results format prescribes.

A person or firm registered under the SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations to publish research, which the rules define to include buy, sell or hold recommendations, price or stop-loss targets, model portfolios and trading calls. Anyone selling those needs this registration; this site gives none of them.

A person or firm registered under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations to give personalised investment advice for a fee, acting as a fiduciary. Generic information through a medium open to the public is not investment advice, and trading calls fall under the research-analyst rules.
An order generated by automated logic rather than typed by a person; under SEBI’s retail algo framework every client order sent through a broker API counts as one and is tagged.
The unique identifier an exchange assigns to a registered algorithm; it travels on every order so the exchange can trace, audit or kill-switch that algo.
A vendor or fintech that lets clients place algo orders through a broker’s API; not regulated by SEBI directly but empanelled with the exchange and acting as the broker’s agent.
A broker’s programmatic interface for orders, positions and prices. Access needs an API key, two-factor login and, for self-hosted algos, a whitelisted static IP.
An algo whose logic the user cannot see or replicate; its provider must be a SEBI-registered research analyst and may not change the logic without fresh registration.
An algo whose rules are fully disclosed and replicable, such as TWAP or VWAP execution; registered on the exchange’s faster track.
The order-rate measure exchanges use to decide whether a self-coded retail algo must be registered; the threshold is {{fact:algo-order-rate-threshold}}.
NSE’s label for a retail client who codes and hosts an algo on a whitelisted static IP; registration is needed only above the order-rate threshold.
A fixed public internet address the broker whitelists so API orders can be traced to one client; mandatory for self-hosted algos at every broker since {{fact:algo-framework-effective-date}}.
An emergency control that cancels pending orders and blocks new ones from a given algo ID (exchange level) or disables a trading segment for the client (broker level).
Orders placed divided by trades executed; exchanges penalise members whose algos post very high ratios, exempting orders close to the last traded price.

Renting rack space inside the exchange’s data centre for the lowest latency; at NSE a full rack lists at {{fact:algo-nse-colo-full-rack}} before connectivity and message-rate charges, which puts it out of retail reach.
Backtesting by optimising on one window and testing on the next, rolled through time, so parameters are always judged on data they did not see.
Using information in a backtest that was not available at the simulated decision time, such as a day’s close to decide that day’s entry.
Average result per trade after costs: win rate × average win minus loss rate × average loss. Positive expectancy is the minimum condition for a tradeable method.
The share of trades closed at a profit. Meaningless without the win-to-loss size ratio: a method that wins seven times in ten still loses money if its losers are three times its winners.
Planned profit distance divided by stop distance at entry; a one-to-two trade risks one rupee to make two.
A trade’s profit or loss divided by the rupees risked at entry (one R is the planned loss at the stop), so trades of different sizes can be compared.
The fall from an equity peak to the next trough as a share of the peak. A fifty per cent drawdown needs a hundred per cent gain to recover.
Choosing shares or lots so the loss at the stop equals a fixed share of equity (commonly one per cent). For bought options, size on the premium at risk, not the notional.

The bet fraction that maximises long-run growth: the win probability minus the loss probability divided by the payoff ratio. Traders use a fraction of it because the inputs are estimates and full Kelly brings deep drawdowns.
A pre-set rupee or R loss after which the trader stops for the day; a control against revenge trading, not a forecast.
Entering new, usually larger, unplanned trades to win back a fresh loss. SEBI’s studies show losses concentrating among the most active traders.
Trading more often or larger than the plan allows. Costs rise with frequency, and SEBI’s studies link higher activity to a higher share of loss-makers.
A record of every trade’s setup, size, entry, exit, R-multiple and notes, reviewed weekly to find what actually makes money.

Under the Income-tax Act 2025 a purchase or sale settled without delivery is a speculative transaction, so intraday equity profit is speculative business income; exchange-traded F&O is carved out and taxed as non-speculative business income. The split decides how losses are used: a speculation loss only against speculation profit, carried forward {{fact:tax-spec-loss-carry-forward}}; an F&O loss against most other income, carried forward {{fact:tax-nonspec-loss-carry-forward}}.

The twelve months beginning in April that the Income-tax Act 2025 uses in place of the previous-year and assessment-year pair; the Act applies from tax year 2026-27, having come into force on {{fact:tax-act-in-force}}.
For the audit test, the sum of the absolute profits and losses on derivative trades (plus option premium received on sale where it is not already counted), not the contract value.

A compulsory audit of the books when business turnover crosses the threshold, {{fact:tax-audit-threshold-digital}} where almost all receipts and payments are digital and a tenth of that otherwise, or when a presumptive-scheme user declares a lower profit than the scheme deems.

Tax paid during the year once the liability is at least {{fact:tax-advance-tax-threshold}}, in cumulative instalments of {{fact:tax-advance-tax-q1}}, {{fact:tax-advance-tax-q2}}, {{fact:tax-advance-tax-q3}} and {{fact:tax-advance-tax-q4}}; presumptive-scheme taxpayers pay {{fact:tax-advance-tax-presumptive}}.

A scheme under {{fact:tax-presumptive-section}} letting an eligible resident declare {{fact:tax-presumptive-rate-digital}} of digital turnover and {{fact:tax-presumptive-rate-other}} of other turnover as profit without keeping books, up to a turnover of {{fact:tax-presumptive-limit}}. Declaring a loss instead triggers books and audit, and opting out locks the trader out for five years.
A mutual fund or ETF that holds an index’s constituents in index weights, competing on expense ratio and tracking difference.

The annual cost deducted from a scheme’s NAV as a share of assets. SEBI caps the base ratio of index funds and ETFs at {{fact:inv-index-fund-ter-cap}}; one Nifty 50 fund charges {{fact:inv-nifty50-ter-direct}} in its direct plan and {{fact:inv-nifty50-ter-regular}} in its regular plan.
A mutual-fund plan with no distributor commission: the same portfolio as the regular plan with a lower expense ratio, bought from the fund house or a direct platform.

The gap between a fund’s return and its index’s return over a period, mostly the expense ratio plus cash drag; SEBI requires monthly disclosure over several horizons. Lower is better, and it captures costs that TER alone misses.
The annualised standard deviation of daily return differences between fund and index; SEBI caps it at {{fact:inv-tracking-error-cap}} for equity index funds and ETFs.
Fixed periodic purchases of fund units. It automates discipline and averages the entry price, but it does not raise the expected return or remove market risk.
The order of returns changes the outcome for anyone adding or withdrawing money: late bad years hurt savers most, early bad years hurt retirees most.

A rules-based index that selects or weights stocks by a trait such as momentum, quality, low volatility or value. NSE factsheets show back-filled history from before launch, which flatters the record.
Splitting money across equity, debt and gold by goals and risk, then periodically selling what rose and buying what fell to restore the split.
An exchange-traded fund backed by physical gold, the main listed route to gold now that new sovereign gold bond issues have stopped; listed units are taxed as long-term after twelve months.

Government bonds priced in grams of gold that pay a small annual interest. No new tranche has been issued since February 2024 and the scheme is in run-off with RBI premature-redemption windows. Capital-gains exemption on redemption: {{fact:inv-sgb-redemption-exemption}}.

Listed business trusts owning income-producing real estate or infrastructure. They must distribute at least {{fact:inv-reit-distribution-min}} of net distributable cash flows, and distributions keep their character (interest, dividend, rent) in the investor’s hands.
Under the Income-tax Act 2025, a fund with more than sixty-five per cent in debt and money-market instruments. Gains on units bought on or after {{date:2023-04-01}}: {{fact:tax-debt-fund-rule}}.
Total listed market value divided by nominal GDP, about {{fact:inv-mcap-to-gdp}} for India at the end of October 2026; a slow-moving valuation context, not a timing tool.
The Bogleheads core of a total US stock fund, a total international stock fund and a bond fund, held at low cost and rebalanced.
Size, value, profitability and investment factors that, together with the market, explain much of the cross-section of stock returns in academic data.
Antonacci’s rule set: pick the stronger of two equity indices by twelve-month return (relative momentum) and hold it only if it beat Treasury bills (absolute momentum), otherwise hold bonds.
Price divided by ten-year average inflation-adjusted earnings; its inverse is a rough estimate of long-run real return.

The RBI scheme under which a resident individual may send up to {{fact:glb-lrs-limit}} abroad per financial year for permitted purposes, including buying foreign shares and ETFs, declared to the bank on Form A2. Unused foreign exchange must come back within {{fact:glb-lrs-idle-funds-days}} days unless it is reinvested.

Tax the bank collects on LRS remittances above {{fact:glb-tcs-threshold}} a year, at {{fact:glb-tcs-rate}} for investment and {{fact:glb-tcs-rate-education-medical}} for education or medical purposes; a pre-paid tax credited in Form 26AS and adjusted or refunded in the return.

The IRS form certifying non-US status so that treaty withholding applies: {{fact:glb-us-dividend-withholding-dtaa}} on dividends for Indian residents instead of {{fact:glb-us-dividend-withholding-default}}. Validity: {{fact:glb-w8ben-validity}}.
The 1989 India–US tax treaty. Its dividend article caps withholding for portfolio holders at {{fact:glb-us-dividend-withholding-dtaa}}, and its relief article lets India credit the US tax paid.
Credit for US tax withheld against the Indian tax on the same income, claimed by filing Form 67 before the return; capped at the Indian tax on that income.

Property the IRS treats as located in the US for estate tax: US real estate and shares of US companies, including US-listed ETFs. A non-resident alien’s US-situs estate is taxable above {{fact:glb-us-estate-exemption-nra}}, at rates reaching {{fact:glb-us-estate-top-rate}}.

An EU-regulated fund, often Ireland-domiciled, that holds US stocks. Its shares are not US-situs property, the Irish fund pays a reduced treaty rate of US dividend withholding, and accumulating share classes reinvest dividends inside the fund so the Indian holder reports no yearly dividend income.

The foreign-assets schedule in ITR-2 and ITR-3 that an ordinarily resident taxpayer must complete for foreign shares, ETFs and bank or broker accounts. Omission can trigger a Black Money Act penalty of {{fact:glb-schedule-fa-rule}}, waived where non-immovable foreign assets total no more than twice that.
NSE Clearing’s daily report of open interest held by clients, DIIs, FPIs and proprietary desks, long and short, by instrument type; read for who is positioned where, not for direction on its own.

A vendor estimate of the aggregate gamma held by dealers, computed from option open interest and used to argue whether hedging will dampen or amplify moves. Published only for US markets; for India it is lore without a public dataset.
The documented tendency to sell winners too early and hold losers too long, because a realised loss hurts more than a paper loss; the behavioural root of averaging down.

Doubling the stake after each loss to recover it. With a finite account and a maximum position size the sequence ends in ruin with certainty, which is why averaging down into a losing leveraged trade is the fastest way to a margin call.
